formulas.name: Switching
f: message switching: store-and-forward the whole message
packet switching: data in packets — datagram or virtual circuit
notes: Tip: Packet switching suits bursty computer data (the Internet).

formulas.name: OSI & TCP/IP models
f: OSI: physical, data link, network, transport, session,
notes: Tip: Repeater / hub → layer 1; bridge / switch → layer 2 (MAC address); router → layer 3 (IP address); gateway → up to layer 7 (protocol conversion).
TNPSC / ESE / APGENCO PYQ: TNPSC PG Q181

formulas.name: Data link control
f: Framing, flow control (stop-and-wait, sliding window), error
notes: Tip: Stop-and-wait efficiency = 1/(1 + 2a), a = propagation time / frame transmission time.
TNPSC / ESE / APGENCO PYQ: TNPSC PG Q184 · ESE 2026 Q134

formulas.name: BISYNC, SDLC, HDLC
notes: Tip: HDLC frame: flag | address | control | information | FCS | flag; modes NRM, ARM, ABM.

formulas.name: Media access (MAC) protocols
f: CSMA/CD: listen, transmit, detect collision → jam → binary
notes: Tip: CSMA/CD needs frame time ≥ 2 × propagation delay to detect collisions.

formulas.name: Ethernet & Arcnet
notes: Where: CSMA/CD = carrier sense multiple access with collision detection; MAC = hardware address
Tip: Arcnet's fixed access time suits industrial control networks.

terms.mean: Listen before talking, stop and back off on collision (Ethernet).
Insert a 0 after five 1s so data never looks like the flag.
Forwards packets between networks using IP addresses (layer 3).
Connects networks that use different protocols.

mistakes.m: TCP and IP work at the same layer
mistakes.c: IP is the network layer (3); TCP is the transport layer (4).

mistakes.m: A hub and a switch are the same
mistakes.c: A hub repeats to every port (layer 1); a switch forwards by MAC address (layer 2).

mistakes.m: Circuit switching suits bursty data best
mistakes.c: Packet switching suits bursty data; circuit switching suits continuous traffic (telephony).

mcqs.q: Q1. A router works at the OSI
mcqs.ans: Ans: (c) Network layer Uses IP addresses.
Ans: (b) CSMA/CD Carrier sense, collision detection.
Ans: (b) 01111110 Bit stuffing keeps data from imitating it.

mcqs.q: Q4. Number of layers in the OSI model
mcqs.ans: Ans: (d) 7 Physical, data link, network, transport, session, presentation, application.

mcqs.q: Q5. A router works at which OSI layer?
mcqs.ans: Ans: (c) Network (3) Routers forward packets by IP address (layer 3); bridges and switches work at layer 2.
Ans: (b) Bit-oriented HDLC uses the flag 01111110 with bit stuffing; BISYNC is character-oriented.

mcqs.q: Q7. Maximum throughput of pure ALOHA
mcqs.ans: Ans: (c) 18.4 % S<sub>max</sub> = 1/(2e) = 0.184; slotted ALOHA doubles it to 1/e = 0.368.

mcqs.q: Q8. Length of an Ethernet MAC address
mcqs.ans: Ans: (a) 48 bits 6 bytes, written as 12 hex digits.
Ans: (d) Connection-oriented and reliable TCP sets up a connection and retransmits lost segments; UDP does not.

ch.takeaway: OSI has 7 layers (bridge → layer 2, router → layer 3, gateway → up to 7). Ethernet uses CSMA/CD; HDLC is bit-oriented with flag 01111110; slotted ALOHA 36.8 %, pure 18.4 %.
